title: 1962 AHSME Problem 27
statement: Let \(a\mathbin{@}b\) represent the operation on two numbers, \(a\) and \(b,\) which selects the larger of the two numbers, with \(a\mathbin{@}a=a.\) Let \(a\mathbin{!}b\) represent the operation which selects the smaller of the two numbers, with \(a\mathbin{!}a=a.\) Which of the following three rules is (are) correct? \[ \begin{aligned} (1)\quad&a\mathbin{@}b=b\mathbin{@}a,\\ (2)\quad&a\mathbin{@}(b\mathbin{@}c)=(a\mathbin{@}b)\mathbin{@}c,\\ (3)\quad&a\mathbin{!}(b\mathbin{@}c)\\ &\quad=(a\mathbin{!}b)\mathbin{@}(a\mathbin{!}c). \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
Maximum is commutative and associative, so \((1)\) and \((2)\) hold. Rule \((3)\) is the distributive identity \[ \begin{aligned} &\min(a,\max(b,c))\\ &\quad=\max(\min(a,b),\min(a,c)). \end{aligned} \] If \(a\ge\max(b,c),\) both sides equal \(\max(b,c);\) if \(a\lt\max(b,c),\) both sides equal \(a.\) Thus \((3)\) also holds.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Translate \(\mathbin{@}\) as maximum and \(\mathbin{!}\) as minimum
For rule \((3),\) compare both sides separately when \(a\) is below or above \(\max(b,c)\)
